Property transfer after a death

The owner of record has died and the heir needs to become the deed owner. Each step is listed in order; tick it off as it is done. The deed itself is drafted on https://2ndchinc.org/staff/deeds/.

This is a checklist, not legal advice. This tool organizes the facts and documents for counsel; it does not decide the route or approve a filing. Check each step against the official forms and statutes linked on it, and ask the Probate Division staff, the Self-Represented Litigant Center or counsel when unsure.

What's next

The property

Heirs and others who may have a share

With no will, list the owner's surviving spouse (if any) and every child, and the children of any child who has died. Parents, brothers and sisters and more distant relatives are heirs only when there is no spouse and no descendant, so do not list aunts, uncles or cousins when children are living (Illinois Probate Act, section 2-1: confirm with the Probate Division). Do list a person when unsure whether a child exists. With a will, also list everyone the will names. A name left off can undo the transfer later.

Return address on the envelopes (the person sending the notices; blank uses the first person listed)

Death certificate

Upload the certified copy (PDF or photo). This page does not read the certificate: someone reads the file and types the fields below, and each one should be checked against the paper. Only the last four digits of the Social Security number are typed into the fields. The uploaded certificate itself is the original and still shows everything on it: it stays in a private staff-only folder, is shared only with counsel, and a redacted copy is needed for anything filed publicly.

Court costs

  • Filing a new estate: $479 (with or without a will) per the Clerk's Probate Division page. The older fee schedule (CCP 0607, 2022) also lists a $250 appearance fee for some case types, so confirm the total when you file.
  • Certified death certificates: $17 for the first copy and $6 for each additional copy ordered together (the posted request form), before any service or delivery fee.
  • Filing the will itself: no fee. Certified copies (of the letters, death certificate): extra, per copy.
  • Newspaper publication (notice to creditors, 3 weeks) and surety bond: the price varies; get a quote and write it in the step note.
  • Recording the deed at the Clerk's Recordings office: a recording fee; ask the office.
  • If you cannot pay: ask the Clerk about a fee waiver (Supreme Court Rule 298), and see the Clerk's filing costs page.
Courts: Probate Division 312-603-6441 · Self-Represented Litigant Center (872) 529-1093 · e-filing help (312) 603-5030. Fees change; confirm with the Clerk before filing.
